data.source_title: The effect of discharge destination and primary insurance provider on hospital discharge delays among patients with traumatic brain injury: a multicenter study of 1,543 patients
data.locator: Abstract, Methods/Results; Results, Discharge delays; Table 1. Discharge delay defined as discharge >=24 hours after case-management documentation that patient was ready.
data.source_setting: Four Level I trauma centers in three US states; adults with TBI and Injury Severity Score >=9.
data.source_n: 1,543 patients total; 210 (13.6%, rounded in abstract to 14%) experienced discharge delay. Reason counts use 210 delayed patients as denominator and can overlap.
data.quantity: Reported delay reasons among delayed patients
data.unit: percent of patients with discharge delay; overlapping reasons
data.source_evidence_basis: Retrospective multicenter patient cohort with medical-record abstraction. Table 1 gives insurance authorization 109/210 (51.9%, rounded in abstract to 52%), no accepting bed 85/210 (40.5%, rounded to 41%), patient-related reasons 72/210 (34.3%, rounded to 34%). Reasons overlap.
data.limitations: Restricted to adult moderate/severe TBI at four trauma centers and delays >=24 hours after documented readiness. Reason assignment is record-based and overlapping; it is not a PA response-time measure or a general all-hospital rate. Not RWJ data.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent post-acute placement authorization separately from acceptance/bed availability after clinical readiness. Use the 52% as a contextual blocker category among delayed TBI cases only, not as an individual probability or PA duration.
